correctness.rationale: Writing the squared norm as the maximum of the strip quadratic Q_s and Euclidean quadratic Q_e avoids differentiating at nonsmooth corners. For arbitrary unit x,y, select active quadratics at x and y. Equal branch choices cancel all linear terms. A mixed strip/Euclidean choice has linear term H=(lambda^2-1)x_1y_1-x_2y_2, whose negative magnitude is bounded by max_{0<=t<=1/lambda}((lambda-lambda^{-1})t+q sqrt(1-t^2)). The unconstrained maximizer is t=q, producing lambda q when lambda<=sqrt(2); after the constraint becomes active, the maximum is 2q^2. This gives an exact lower slope for S^2. Strict mixed-branch unit vectors approaching the relevant boundary attain the same coefficient in the limit, proving the right derivative. The square-root step gives the stated coefficient and both branches agree at lambda=sqrt(2).
